card.name: Words introducing a drug given to subjects
card.fires_on: Linking verbs or prepositions such as receiving, given, received, following, by or of that come right before the name of a drug being given. Mostly in interaction studies and animal or volunteer trials.

modes.label: Receiving or given
modes.description: A verb meaning a subject was given a drug, placed just before the drug name.
modes.example: In healthy subjects who were<< given>> a single oral 600 mg

modes.label: Linking word in interaction findings
modes.description: A small linking word before a co-administered drug in an interaction result.
modes.example: The T 1/2 and T max of buspirone were not significantly affected<< by>> diltiazem.

modes.label: Concomitant administration
modes.description: The end of the word concomitant, ahead of administration of another drug.
modes.example: Drug Interactions A 30 to 45% increase in AUC and C max of nisoldipine was observed with concom<<itant>> administration of cimetidine 40

card.writes: It seems to prepare the model to write the name of a drug, which is often a rare or unusual name.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a text says who was given which drug, just before the drug name.
